messages:
Anna (Support): Hey team — ACME's private VPC is failing calls to api.redwood.com via their corporate proxy. They see CONNECT / TLS errors and 403s. Happening from eu-west-1. Sam pasted repro below. Can Eng/NetOps take a look?

Sam (ACME): Repro steps:
1) From a bastion inside customer VPC: 
   curl -v --proxy http://corp-proxy.corp:8080 https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings 
Output: 
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings
* Hostname was NOT found in DNS cache
*   Trying 10.0.0.45:8080... connected
> CONNECT api.redwood.com:443 HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.com
> Proxy-Connection: Keep-Alive
>
< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established
* Proxy replied OK to CONNECT request
* Establishing TLS connection to api.redwood.com
* SSL: certificate subject name 'internal-proxy.corp' does not match 'api.redwood.com'
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca

Sam (ACME): They also tried openssl to inspect the cert returned through the proxy: 
printf "CONNECT api.redwood.com:443 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api.redwood.com\r\n\r\n" | nc corp-proxy.corp 8080 | openssl s_client -servername api.redwood.com -showcerts 
Result shows the presented cert CN=internal-proxy.corp (MITM appliance cert).

Miguel (Eng): Sounds like the proxy is doing TLS interception (MITM) and presenting its own cert. Two possible causes for the error stack:
- Proxy is intercepting CONNECT and terminating TLS (explicit MITM). SNI is likely visible to the proxy and it reissues a new cert.
- Or the proxy is rewriting headers or DNS so the CONNECT is routed to an internal gateway that doesn't support HTTPS passthrough.

Kai (NetOps): Quick DNS check from their bastion? If proxy does DNS interception, api.redwood.com might resolve to an internal IP.

Sam (ACME): Dug in — dig output: 
$ dig +short api.redwood.com 
10.10.50.5
That IP space is internal to their egress cluster. They confirmed their proxy returns that IP for outbound lookups.

Kai (NetOps): That confirms it. Their proxy is doing egress DNS rewrite + TLS intercept. Two failure modes: cert mismatch (client rejects MITM cert) or proxy enforces a policy to only allow CONNECT to certain SNI values and returns 403 for others.

Miguel (Eng): For repro / triage we should have them do minimal checks to pin the root cause:
- Curl with verbose to show CONNECT vs TLS error (they already did).
- Test direct TCP CONNECT pass-through using netcat to see if proxy accepts raw CONNECT and proxies traffic: 
  printf "CONNECT api.redwood.com:443 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api.redwood.com\r\n\r\n" | nc corp-proxy.corp 8080 -w 5 
  then try to send raw TLS ClientHello bytes (or pipe openssl s_client) to see if we get server hello from Redwood.
- openssl s_client via the proxy: 
  printf "CONNECT api.redwood.com:443 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api.redwood.com\r\n\r\n" | nc corp-proxy.corp 8080 | openssl s_client -servername api.redwood.com -connect api.redwood.com:443
If you get internal-proxy cert, it's MITM.

Kai (NetOps): Also ask their security team if they have a "TLS decrypt" policy or an "egress allowlist" that only allows passthrough for some domains. Common enterprise appliances will either: 1) allow CONNECT (tunnel) transparently, 2) allow CONNECT but terminate TLS (MITM), or 3) forbid CONNECT to certain hosts and return 403.

Anna (Support): What should we ask customer to change to get unblocked quickly?

Miguel (Eng): Short-term workarounds:
- If they can, add api.redwood.com to the proxy's TLS-exempt/bypass list (no MITM) or to the CONNECT allowlist.
- Alternatively, allowlist Redwood public egress IPs so the proxy can forward without intercepting — we maintain a list of IP ranges (we'll provide).
- Use a private endpoint or VPC-peering option (if they have Private deployment) — not always possible.

Anna (Support): We'll need to provide the IP ranges + cert fingerprint for verification. Miguel, can you generate the thumbprint?

Miguel (Eng): Sure. From our edge cert (api.redwood.com) the SHA256 fingerprint is: 
SHA256 Fingerprint=AB:3C:7F:1D:9A:...:E4 (example)
Run on their side if they capture cert: 
  openssl x509 -in cert.pem -noout -fingerprint -sha256
I'll attach canonical IP ranges in the ticket.

Sam (ACME): Their SecOps says they can add exceptions but need exact values and some repro logs. They're going to try adding a no-MITM rule for api.redwood.com and report back.

Kai (NetOps): Extra note: if their proxy rewrites Host headers (or injects headers) that shouldn't affect CONNECT because CONNECT tunnels raw TCP after the 200. But some transparent proxies rewrite or intercept at L7 and will break the tunnel. If they have an HTTP gateway in front of the proxy that rewrites SNI to an internal FQDN, they'll need to disable that behavior for our hostname.

Anna (Support): Sam, please update when SecOps toggles the bypass. If they still fail, capture a tcpdump of the CONNECT handshake and attach (pcap) so Eng can see if SNI is being stripped or modified.

Sam (ACME): Will do. Quick question: any chance our SDKs can detect MITM and surface a clearer error? Right now it's a generic TLS error.

Miguel (Eng): We can add a clearer error mapping for cert-subject mismatch (detect when the presented cert CN != expected host and return a diagnostic hint about TLS interception / proxy MITM). Filed internal ticket RD-4998 to add guidance and sample troubleshooting commands.

DeployBot: Deployment RD-4998 created by miguel at 1968022024.

Anna (Support): Thanks all — marking this thread monitoring. Sam, we'll stand by for the bypass change and pcap. If they need more immediate unblock, we can provide an ephemeral IP allowlist for their test window.

Sam (ACME): SecOps added api.redwood.com to bypass list, re-ran curl and now: 
* Connected to 3.222.100.45 (api.redwood.com) port 443
* TLS handshake completed
* HTTP/2 200
Works! Thanks folks.

Anna (Support): Great — closing for now, will follow up once RD-4998 lands to give better telemetry to customers. :)
